title: Building glotworld.com to gamify language learning - German
author: gokkai
selftext:
hey r/aigamedev, 

\~20 year exp dev, working on my arch nemesis: German Language. Before AI was a thing I was proud of myself because I could learn a completely new tech stack in \~2 weeks, but doesn't matter how hard I tried I couldn't manage to keep myself focused at learning German language. 

I was fiddling around with the idea of some mini-games with sprites in the last months and with the sprite generation capabilities of ChatGPT ImageGEN and Opus 5.5, suddenly my output got a huge uptick. I think the last time I had a similar uptick was when Cursor and ChatGPT3.5 became a thing. 

Anyways here it is [https://glotworld.com/](https://glotworld.com/),

\- From A0 to B1, with mysteries, interesting characters and mini-games.

\- Free to play for \~2 hr sessions. You need to pay only if you want to save your progress after 2 hours(of if you like the game ofc :) ).

\- Lots and lots of content, voiceover with QWEN TTS.

\- Sentence based learning by highlighting words.

\- Icons next to nouns to trigger visual memory.

\- Spaced repetition and more...

Compared to all the other times when I tried to learn German by other means from going to Goethe Institute course to trying Duolingo, Babbel etc, this felt the best to spend time on and learn while tricking my brain into thinking that it's playing a game :) 

I'm still not 100% sold on the character set or the funkiness of the artwork, I'm open for suggestions or techniques to have more consistency. But it has it's own charm.

What worked really well,

1 - Chatgpt imagegen for environments, objects, buildings.

2 - Claude Opus 5.5 and fable for story and game engine. 

What didn't work,

1 - Chatgpt imagegen for any kind of animated sprites.

2 - Astra or Sol 6, 6.1 for any kind of game engine or story development.
